content: test(realtime): fold a GPT-Live delegated call landing in the next reply into SIM-18

Register a GPT-Live delegated tool call recorded in the next reply as a realtime simulator finding This adds a GPT-Live violation that #9834's CI exploration hit to the realtime simulator's known findings, as part of SIM-18. Tests only. The `test_exploration[gpt-live]` run on one CI shard failed with `response.mixed`: "the response at 2 holds what server responses [1, 2] said". The minimal repro, which is deterministic on `main`: ``` sim.delegate(); sim.backend_call(); sim.backend_finish(); sim.advance_time(0.1); sim.finish_tool() sim.speak(); sim.backend_call(); sim.settle() ``` A delegation's backend calls one tool and finishes, then calls a second tool after the model has started speaking a new reply. The session records that second call in the new reply's `ModelResponse` (`[SpeechPart('r2w1'), ToolCallPart('call_2')]`), although it belongs to the delegated response. With words before it, those words are recorded in the wrong response as well (`response.truncated`). This is SIM-18's mechanism: the session can't continue a response it has already recorded, so what a delegated response adds later goes into whatever response it is building at that point. SIM-18 already covers the case where nothing else is spoken in between (`response.duplicated`). So I added `response.mixed` and `response.truncated` to its codes, extended its title, and pinned this scenario as a second strict expected failure. Per-response-id state, the fix SIM-18 tracks, retires both. The full CI trace now classifies as SIM-18. - Part of the realtime session refactor's simulator work; no issue. ### Checklist - [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md). - [x] Any permitted **compatibility impact** has a label, warning, migration, release note, and exact API-check waiver. - [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

🟡 **Medium** `simulation/_findings.py:761` `SIM-18` now suppresses unrelated `response.mixed` and `response.truncated` violations whenever any GPT-Live response continued after a tool call. `matching_findings()` evaluates this predicate for each violation, but `_continued_after_calling()` scans all truth responses and ignores that violation, so unrelated mixed or truncated responses are misclassified as `SIM-18` instead of being reported as new findings. Remove these codes until the predicate is scoped to the current violation. ```suggestion codes=frozenset({'response.duplicated'}), ```

test(realtime): match SIM-18's mixed and truncated responses only on a response the violation names

Agreed: the predicate scanned every response, so any GPT-Live response that continued after a call would have excused an unrelated `response.mixed` or `response.truncated`. Fixed in 949e0c5ae. For those two codes, SIM-18 now matches only when one of the responses the violation names (via `_context_responses`) continued after its first tool call. `response.duplicated` keeps the original whole-trace check, since its context names the split response's pieces rather than the response.

The CI trace still classifies as SIM-18 for all three codes. A mixed or truncated response that names no continued response no longer matches.

In d6eef23b4 SIM-18 is scoped the same way for all three codes: it matches only when a response the violation names continued after its first tool call. The CI trace, SIM-18's two pins and a 2500-example GPT-Live exploration all still classify as before.
